title: Matrix Product Operators In The Age of Block Encoding
abstract: We develop a block-encoding compiler that speeds up linear combination of unitaries Hamiltonian simulation programs by treating matrix product operators as compressed, virtual-path LCU programs. In showing how these new conditional PREP and SELECT stages are compiled in terms of a parent matrix product operator, we go beyond typical operator splitting product formulas and illustrate how tensor networks are a natural language and valid intermediate representation for quantum circuits. Our results are numerically verified for two important cases, namely, Heisenberg and perturbed Heisenberg-adjacent chain real-time evolution, and highlight polynomial speedups. Specifically, we highlight a polynomial speedup that avoids the $\mathcal{O}(N^K)$ Pauli-string growth when the compressed MPO bond dimension and path normalization remain mild. We quantify how MPO truncation error and bond-dimension budgets affect the compiled polynomial representation. Our algorithms show how classical pre-processing in terms of tensor network data structures opens new avenues to accelerate quantum algorithms.
summary: This work introduces a block-encoding compiler that treats Matrix Product Operators (MPOs) as natural intermediate representations for quantum circuits. It significantly accelerates Hamiltonian simulation by compiling the time evolution operator directly within the MPO structure, avoiding exponential resource scaling associated with explicit Pauli expansions.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently compiling quantum circuits for simulating time evolution generated by Hamiltonians expressed as Matrix Product Operators (MPOs). It aims to improve upon standard methods that suffer from exponential resource scaling.
main_result: A novel MPO block-encoding compiler achieves polynomial speedups by treating MPOs as structured intermediate representations, thereby avoiding the prohibitive $\mathcal{O}(NK)$ Pauli-string growth seen in explicit expansions.
method: The core method involves developing a block-encoding compiler that maps MPOs to conditional PREP and SELECT stages within a Linear Circuit Unit (LCU) framework. This allows for compiling polynomial transformations directly at the MPO level.
model_or_system: The focus is on real-time quantum Hamiltonian simulation, exemplified by the Heisenberg model and its perturbed variants. The underlying mathematical structure is the representation of time evolution unitaries ($e^{-itH}$) using tensor networks (MPOs).
key_observables: Computational cost scaling, MPO bond dimension ($\chi$), Pauli-string growth rate, and the normalization overhead factor ($\alpha$).
important_parameters: Bond dimension ($\chi$), truncation error, system size ($N$), and Taylor expansion order ($K$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that classical pre-processing using tensor network data structures can accelerate quantum algorithms. It compares different compilation routes (Pauli vs. MPO-transition).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scaling of MPO bond dimension ($\chi$) independent of system size for Hamiltonian powers, and compare relative Frobenius errors when synthesizing unitaries via MPO Taylor expansions.
paper_structure: The paper develops a block-encoding compiler by first mapping MPOs to LCU structures. It then compares this MPO-transition route against explicit Pauli expansion routes, demonstrating polynomial speedups in resource scaling for simulating time evolution.
why_interesting: For AMO physicists studying open quantum systems or dynamics, the ability to efficiently simulate complex Hamiltonians like Heisenberg models using tensor network formalisms is crucial for accessing regimes where standard methods fail due to exponential overheads.
